content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Larry Poindexter, the veteran character actor best known as by-the-book LAPD Captain Tom Fuller in the 2003 film S.W.A.T., has died at 66.

Poindexter died on the morning of November 18, 2026, four and a half days after being hit by a car while crossing a street in his Studio City neighborhood on Friday night to pick up food. He had been in the hospital since the accident and was scheduled to have surgery for broken ribs on Tuesday when he died suddenly that morning, according to Deadline.

Born December 16, 1959, in Dallas, Texas, Poindexter's acting career spanned more than four decades and nearly 200 movies and television series. His best-known film role came in 2003's S.W.A.T., where his Captain Fuller went head-to-head with Samuel L. Jackson's Hondo. On television, he was a series regular on the MTV comedy The Hard Times of RJ Berger and had a major recurring role on CBS' JAG as Dalton Lowne. He appeared in 30 episodes of Days of Our Lives, playing Ben Welch in 1984 and Father Louis from 2014 to 2018, along with a 23-episode stint on Santa Barbara and 12 episodes of General Hospital. He also played Sergeant Boyer in the S.W.A.T. television series, and his dozens of guest roles included Quantum Leap, NYPD Blue, Friends, How I Met Your Mother, Will & Grace, NCIS, Scandal, CSI: Miami, Hawaii Five-0, Castle, Curb Your Enthusiasm, Supernatural, Bones, The Rookie and 9-1-1. His most recent guest appearance was in Season 4 of The Lincoln Lawyer earlier this year.

Poindexter was also a musician, the lead singer of the alternative country band The High Lonesome in the 1990s. The band's album Feel Free To Do So was released in 1995.

Poindexter is survived by his wife, leading casting director Carol Kritzer, and their two sons.

Sources: Deadline; Wikipedia.
